results.cause: The pod spec runs command ["/app/payment-gateway", "--listen=:8443"] on image "busybox:1.36". The runtime reports "exec: \"/app/payment-gateway\": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory" (StartError, exit 128). Stock busybox does not contain the payment-gateway binary. Most likely the image field points to busybox instead of the real payment-gateway application image. The rule finding says exit 127, but the actual exit code is 128 (StartError). The cause it gives, a missing command, still matches the evidence.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image in deployment/payment-gateway to the actual payment-gateway application image that contains /app/payment-gateway, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<your-payment-gateway-image>:<tag>`.
If the image is correct but the binary sits at a different path, change the command to the real path of the binary in that image.

After the rollout, check the pod with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/payment-gateway`. The Deployment currently shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded, which clears once a new ReplicaSet becomes available.

results.cause: Migration 0042_add_orders_index fails with 'ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists' and exits 1. The index already exists, so the migration is not idempotent and fails on every retry. Note that the init container's args hardcode both the error message and 'exit 1', so as written it fails every time no matter what state the database is in.
fix: Fix the migrate init container's command/args in the orders-api Deployment. Remove the hardcoded 'exit 1', or replace the script with the real migration command.

Make migration 0042_add_orders_index idempotent, e.g. use 'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ...', or mark the migration as already applied in the migration tracking table, since orders_idx already exists.
Apply the change (kubectl apply / kubectl rollout restart deployment/orders-api -n pfa-lab) and confirm migrate exits 0 and api starts.

results.cause: The startup script requires DATABASE_URL and exits when it is empty. The container's env only has DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL. The log confirms it: "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set", followed by exit code 1.
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env in deployment/checkout-api. Because a connection URL usually holds credentials, source it from a Secret, e.g. env: - name: DATABASE_URL valueFrom: secretKeyRef: {name: <your-secret>, key: DATABASE_URL}.
Apply the change and watch the rollout: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api.
Separately, the script echoes the DB password to the logs ("db config: user=$DB_USER password=$DB_PASSWORD"). Remove that line so the credential stops leaking into logs.

results.cause: The tag looks like a typo: "1.36.1-uclbic" instead of the busybox variant "1.36.1-uclibc". The registry answers "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found" (rpc error code = NotFound). The rollout has since hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Fix the image tag in the Deployment: `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc` (or edit spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image).
If you did not intend the uclibc variant, use a tag that exists, e.g. `busybox:1.36.1`. Confirm with `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc`.
Watch the new rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront`.

results.cause: The image field contains two tags: "busybox:1.36:latest". An image reference can have only one ":tag", so the kubelet rejects it with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). This is a spec error, not a registry or credentials problem.
fix: Set the container image to a single tag, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36`, or edit spec.template.spec.containers[name=worker].image to "busybox:1.36" in the manifest or Helm values.
If the tag is assembled from variables (e.g. repo:version plus a default ":latest"), fix the template so only one tag is appended.
Watch the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/notify-worker`. It recovers from ProgressDeadlineExceeded once a new ReplicaSet becomes ready.

results.cause: Pulls go through the registry mirror registry-mirror:1273, which returned "500 Internal Server Error" on the manifest HEAD request for billing/ui:3.2.0 (ns=registry.pfa-lab.invalid). The mirror could not fetch the image from upstream. The most likely reason is that the registry hostname "registry.pfa-lab.invalid" is wrong or unresolvable from the mirror (".invalid" is a reserved TLD that never resolves). Otherwise the mirror itself is failing. This is not a not-found or auth error.
fix: Correct the registry host in the image reference: set spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image to the real registry, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<correct-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0`.

If registry.pfa-lab.invalid really is the intended host, fix the upstream configuration and DNS of the mirror registry-mirror:1273 so it can reach that registry. Check the mirror's logs for the upstream error behind the 500.
As a workaround, pull directly from a reachable registry without the mirror, or preload the image onto the node desktop-control-plane.
After fixing, restart the rollout: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/billing-ui`.

results.cause: The container command ends with "exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0", which allocates 300M. That is more than resources.limits.memory "200Mi". The logs show warmup reaching "cache warmup: loading remaining 100MB" and then "dispatching hogs: 0 cpu, 0 io, 1 vm, 0 hdd", after which the container is terminated with reason OOMKilled, exit code 137. The usage is fixed by the args, not a leak, so the limit is simply too low for what the workload is configured to load.
fix: Raise the memory in the statefulset session-cache container cache to cover the 300M allocation plus overhead, e.g. resources.limits.memory: 384Mi (or the rule's suggested 448Mi), and set resources.requests.memory to match: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"384Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"384Mi"}]'
Alternatively, if 200Mi must stay, reduce the load: change --vm-bytes 300M in the container args to something well under the limit (e.g. 150M).
If the pod does not pick up the change on its own, delete it so the statefulset recreates it with the new spec: kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pod session-cache-0

results.cause: The container command allocates 250M ("exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0", log: "loading 250MB of order history into memory"), roughly double the limits.memory of 128Mi, so it is OOMKilled (exit code 137) immediately every time.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory on container worker in deployment/report-worker to at least 320Mi (250M ≈ 239Mi of data plus runtime headroom), e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=320Mi --requests=memory=256Mi
Alternatively reduce what the job loads at once: lower --vm-bytes (or, for the real app, process the order history in smaller batches) so peak usage stays well under 128Mi
After the change, confirm with kubectl -n pfa-lab get pod -l app=report-worker -w (or the pod name) that restarts stop and the pod becomes Ready

results.cause: The container is configured to hold 200MB in memory (args: "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0", log line "buffering 200MB of logs in memory"), but resources.limits.memory is 64Mi. 200M is about 191Mi, roughly 3x the limit, so the kernel kills it right away (last state: OOMKilled, exit code 137, started and finished at 19:38:27).
fix: Either lower the in-memory buffer below the limit, e.g. change the arg to --vm-bytes 48M so it fits under 64Mi with headroom, or raise the limit to fit the 200MB buffer: set containers[log-shipper].resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) to at least 256Mi.
Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi, or edit the --vm-bytes arg in the deployment spec.
Optional, for a real log shipper: cap its buffer size in config rather than holding 200MB in RAM, and size the limit to buffer size plus runtime overhead.

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores), which is far more than the single node offers. The scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu" and preemption is not helpful. This is almost certainly a unit mistake: 4000 was meant as 4000m (4 cores) or less.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, change spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu from "4000"/"4k" to "4000m", or lower it to what the workload actually needs (e.g. "100m" for a busybox sleep).
Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m. Make sure the value fits within a node's allocatable CPU (check with kubectl describe node).
If the training job really needs many cores, add a node with enough allocatable CPU. A request of 4000 cores will never schedule.

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab. The kubelet has retried the mount 942 times since 2026-11-02 ("MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "templates" : configmap "email-templates" not found"), so the container never starts and the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the right namespace, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>`, or apply its manifest if it lives elsewhere in your repo/chart.
If the configmap exists under a different name, fix spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.name in deployment/email-sender to the correct name and re-apply.
If the templates are optional for startup, set spec.template.spec.volumes[name=templates].configMap.optional: true so the pod can start without it.
After the configmap exists, the kubelet retries the mount automatically. To force a fresh rollout, run `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/email-sender`.

results.cause: The pod spec sets nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, and the scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." The only node in the cluster does not carry the label hardware=gpu-a100. Preemption cannot help ("Preemption is not helpful for scheduling").
fix: If the workload does not need an A100 node (the container only runs busybox:1.36 'sleep 3600'), remove or correct spec.template.spec.nodeSelector.hardware in deployment/video-encoder, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
If the node really is the intended target, check its labels with kubectl get nodes --show-labels and add the label: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
If an A100 node is required, add a node with label hardware=gpu-a100 to the cluster (e.g. a GPU node pool)

results.cause: The readiness probe is "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves /healthz: the container creates /www/healthz and runs "httpd -f -p 80 -h /www", and logs "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz". No /ready file exists, so httpd returns 404 (event Unhealthy x38665). The port (http=80) is correct; only the path is wrong.
fix: Change spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path from /ready to /healthz, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]'
Alternatively, if /ready must stay, have the container create it too (e.g. add 'echo ok > /www/ready' to the startup args).
After the change, confirm rollout: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/catalog-api

results.cause: The liveness probe kills the container during startup. The script runs `sleep 45` before `exec httpd -f -p 80`, so nothing listens on port 80 for 45 seconds. The liveness probe (HTTP /healthz port=http, initial_delay_seconds 2, period_seconds 3, failure_threshold 2) fails after roughly 8 seconds, and the kubelet kills the container. Exit 137 is a SIGKILL, and the reason is 'Error', not 'OOMKilled'. The pod is BestEffort with no memory limit, so OOM is unlikely. The last run lasted 36s (19:38:23 to 19:38:59). That fits a probe kill: `sh` as PID 1 ignores SIGTERM, so the kubelet waits out the default 30s grace period before sending SIGKILL. The logs never reach 'ledger-api listening on :80'. No 'Unhealthy' probe events were included in the evidence, so the probe kill is inferred rather than shown directly.
fix: Add a startupProbe to container api so liveness checks wait until startup is done, e.g. startupProbe: httpGet {path: /healthz, port: http}, periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 15 (allows about 75s, more than the 45s journal replay).
Alternatively, raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds from 2 to at least 60, and consider timeoutSeconds 2-3 and failureThreshold 3.
Add a readinessProbe on HTTP /healthz port http so the pod only receives traffic once httpd is listening.
Apply the change (kubectl apply or kubectl edit deployment/ledger-api -n pfa-lab) and check that the logs reach 'ledger-api listening on :80' and the pod becomes Ready.

results.cause: The liveness probe is "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80" and logs "inventory-api listening on :80". The container declares only port "http=80/TCP". Every probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused". After failure_threshold 2 the kubelet kills the container with exit code 137, even though the app itself did not crash.
fix: In the statefulset inventory-api spec, change containers[api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port from 8080 to 80 (or to the named port "http").

Apply it, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]', then delete pod inventory-api-0 if it does not roll automatically.
Optionally add a readinessProbe on the same port/path so the pod reports Ready.
